skill.name: UI Design System

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged inline backtick spans in SKILL.md as Ruby or shell execution. Manual review shows those spans are CSS values, colors, file paths, and animation names inside Markdown documentation, not executable code. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or other semantic security issue was found.

static_findings.snippet: - **Primary Accent**: `#2d7d6c` (Teal/Greenish) used in buttons and highlights.
- **Cards**: Glassmorphism effect (blur + transparency), rounded corners (`12px` or `16px`).
- **Inputs**: Rounded (`24px`), borderless or subtle border, focus rings.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line is Markdown documentation containing an inline code span for a CSS value, animation name, or file path. There is no Ruby file, shell invocation, or executable context.

content.user_title: Apply a Consistent UI Design System
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent visual rules when building the Physical AI Hub interface. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear theme guidance.
actual_capabilities: Describes the Physical AI Hub dark theme, including gradient background, teal accent, text color, and border style.
Defines typography guidance using Poppins and four weight levels.
Specifies core button, card, input, and dropdown styling rules.
Provides animation guidance for transitions and named keyframes.
Points agents to global, Docusaurus, and module CSS files for implementation.
limitations: Does not include ready-made component code or design token files.
Focuses on one dark visual direction and does not define a light theme.
Does not document accessibility criteria beyond basic readability and focus ring guidance.
Does not include screenshots, spacing scales, or responsive layout rules.

use_cases.title: Style Product Interfaces
use_cases.description: Apply the Physical AI Hub theme while editing CSS or component styles.

use_cases.title: Standardize Visual Rules
use_cases.description: Convert the written visual rules into tokens, component standards, and CSS naming guidance.

use_cases.title: Document UI Standards
use_cases.description: Explain the approved typography, colors, and component behavior in product documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Apply the Theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this UI Design System skill to restyle a page for the Physical AI Hub. Preserve behavior and apply the documented theme, typography, and component rules.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component against the UI Design System skill. List mismatches in colors, typography, cards, inputs, dropdowns, and transitions.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this feature to match the Physical AI Hub dark theme. Use the documented CSS structure when deciding where styles belong.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan for an existing interface using this skill. Prioritize shared CSS, component consistency, animation cleanup, and Docusaurus overrides.

output_examples.input: User asks Claude Code to review a chatbot panel against the skill.
output: The panel uses the approved dark background and teal accent.
The input radius should be rounded to match the documented control style.
Move shared colors into the global CSS layer before changing module styles.

output_examples.input: User asks Codex to plan a Docusaurus theme update.
output_examples.output: The answer identifies the custom CSS file, lists color and typography updates, and notes hover transition checks.

output_examples.input: User asks Claude to summarize the interface style for a new designer.
output_examples.output: The response describes a dark, modern Physical AI Hub interface with Poppins typography, teal accents, glass cards, and smooth transitions.

best_practices: Use the documented colors and typography before adding new visual choices.
Keep shared theme rules in global CSS and isolate complex component styles in modules.
Check hover, focus, and dropdown states after applying animation changes.
anti_patterns: Do not replace the theme with unrelated palettes or fonts.
Do not add one-off component styles when a shared CSS rule fits.
Do not treat the skill as a complete accessibility or layout specification.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents apply the Physical AI Hub visual system to interface work.

faq.question: Can it generate complete components?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance, not complete component implementations.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it only for dark mode?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented palette focuses on a primary dark mode theme.

faq.question: Does it define where CSS should live?
faq.answer: Yes. It points to global CSS, Docusaurus custom CSS, and module CSS usage.

faq.question: Does it require running commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown design reference and does not require command execution.
